newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss "Comi" volume low but Soffex plans no change.
newsitem.headline: Swiss "Comi" volume low but Soffex plans no change.

text.p: Trading in Switzerland's medium-term bond futures, or "Comi" contract, remains slow but the Swiss futures exchange Soffex plans no radical changes in the contract, bourse officials said.
"I would like to see more volume," said Otto Naegeli, a member of the Swiss Stock Exchange management board and in charge of its markets division.
But, he added "We will leave it as it is."

He said the longer-term Confederate, or "Conf" futures contract based on Swiss federal bonds with maturities of eight to 13 years also needed two or three years to get established, implying the Comi may need more time as well.
The Comi, launched on June 21, is based on federal bonds with maturities of three to eight years.
Traded volume in August was 7,933 contracts, compared with 67,779 contracts in the well-established Conf contract, which started trade on Soffex in May 1992.
Trade in the Comi continues to be slow, with only one Comi traded on Monday, for example.
The Comi may have failed to catch on so far partly because of recent declines in Swiss interest rates, which have caused the curve to steepen and created more interest in the long end, traders said.
"The Comi simply has not yet achieved take-off," said Peter Thomann, head of the Swiss Federal Treasury.

Thomann has suggested the Treasury may use futures in its asset and liability management, and when the Comi was introduced in June, he said such a contract offered a welcome opportunity for the market.
"We have many possibilities which we could use," Thomann said. "We want a liquid Treasury market," he added.
He also said it was too early to judge whether the Comi will succeed.
"It is too early to say the Comi has been a disappointment," Thomann said.
